The next day, the Master entered the Sangha hall and said, "Yesterday, my response to the two Dharma brothers was not satisfactory.
I now ask you both to speak it. If you can speak it, I, the old monk, shall open the gruel and stay with you for the summer retreat. Speak quickly!"
The Master said, "The Way is swift. The monk replied, "Life is too precious. The Master then opened the gruel for them to pass the summer retreat together.
The incense burned and all was still, a profound silence; moss covered the vermilion courtyard as the bright moon shone clear. Entering the room, he sat indolently upon the central dais;
going out the door, he was even too lazy to descend the steps.
Chan Master Chuanzi Cheng instructed Jia Shan, saying: "You must ensure that where you hide your body, there are no traces;
and where there are no traces, do not hide your body. For thirty years I was at Yaoshan, and I have clarified only this matter."
White clouds beyond the railing evoke thoughts of vast leisure; Densely woven, they cannot be cut open by golden shears. The secluded cavern holds no intent for golden locks;
Moving freely without restraint, it comes and goes.
A monk asked Qingfeng Chu: "The Great Matter has already been accomplished; why then is it as if one were mourning for a deceased parent?
The Master said: "Without the spring breeze, the flowers do not bloom; yet once they have bloomed, the breeze blows them away."
Upon returning to your ancestral home, do not be negligent; exert all your strength to serve your parents morning and night.
When the mechanism is exhausted and effort forgotten, yet the bond of gratitude and duty is severed, one becomes an unfilial person of icchantika nature.
Chan Master Sheng of Bishu asked Dongshan, "Where have you come from? Dongshan replied, "I have come from being intimate.
The Master said, "If you are intimate, why do you need to move these two pieces of skin [your lips]? Later, when Caoshan heard this account cited, he remarked, "One son has truly attained it."
From the beginning, father and son have never been apart; why trouble a barren woman with further questioning?
Last night, on the shadowless tree of the cold crag, a branch lay bare amidst the depths of white clouds.
Dongshan was once asked by a monk, "The Master teaches students to walk the 'bird-path. I do not know how one walks the bird-path.
The Master said, "One does not encounter a single person. The monk asked, "How does one walk it?
The Master said, "You must simply proceed with no self-interest beneath your feet. The monk asked, "Is walking the bird-path not precisely one's original face? The Master said, "Disciple."
[The student] asked, "Because of what delusion? The Master said, "In what way is the student deluded?
[The student] said, "If one is not deluded, why does one instead mistake a servant for a lord? The Master said, "Why do you ask, 'What is the original face?
The Master said, "Do not walk the path of birds."
The ancient path winds serenely through the vast void; yet to traverse the profound remains a journey over precipices.
Though not ascending the bird-path may be considered subtle, upon close examination, one has already encountered the Way.
Dongshan asked a monk, "What is the most painful thing in the world? The monk replied, "Hell is the most painful. The Master said, "Not so.
To be here, beneath this thread of robes, and not clarify the Great Matter—this is called the greatest suffering."
How many varieties of boiling cauldrons and glowing coals are there? The three paths of the hells are not yet so bitter and sour.
One must believe the intimate words of Xinfeng: do not be negligent beneath the *kāṣāya*.
Shenshan and Dongshan were crossing a single-plank bridge. Dongshan crossed first and, picking up the bridge, said, "Come over here.
Shenshan called out, "Venerable Jia! whereupon Dongshan set the bridge down.
On level ground, one digs a pit without cause; a wooden bridge is lifted up for people to walk upon. How can one cross the deep, cold waters?
At moonlit night, the golden rooster announces the fifth watch.
One day, Chan Master Jianyuan Xing took up a spade and went to Shishuang.
In the Dharma Hall, he walked from east to west and from west to east. Shishuang asked, "What are you doing? The Master replied, "I am seeking the spiritual bones of the former master.

Shishuang said, "The vast waves are immense and white billows overflow the heavens; what spiritual bones of the former master can you seek? The Master said, "This is precisely the time to apply effort."
Shuang said, "In this place, even a needle cannot pierce it; what effort could possibly be applied? The Master took his spade upon his shoulder and went out.
The local ground is luminously clear, devoid of a single thing; how many can recognize the golden bones?
When he supported the spade on his shoulder and walked away, great eloquence has always remained as if stammering.
A monk asked Jia Shan, "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha? The Master said, "You must brandish the sword.
If you do not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in his boat. Later, the same monk asked Shi Sang, "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha?"
Shuang said, "He has no land; where could one meet him? When the monk returned and related this to the Master, the Master said, "In the deployment of the gate, he is not my equal;
yet in entering into the profound discourse on principle, he still falls short of Shishuang by a hundred paces."
A single phrase for the occasion rings like jade; inside and out, its brilliance fills the eyes with cold clarity. One never dwells within the realm of no-outflows;
it would be difficult to perceive it even within the shadows of the moon’s radiance.
A monk asked Jia Shan, "What is the realm of Jia Shan? The Master said, "The monkey carries its young back behind the green peaks;
the bird holds a falling flower before the azure cliffs."
The clam holds the bright moon; the pearl is born within its belly. The dragon embraces the deep clouds; rain falls upon the void.
Do not stir up great waves across the level fields; you must simply let every drop flow toward the east.
A monk asked Jia Shan, "I do not ask about the place where one has attained realization; I pray for a word from the Master regarding the place where one has not yet realized.
The Master said, "The door hangs in the withered forest; discern it within the shadows."
Beyond the limit of majestic sound, one cannot travel; casting off the hand, returning home, there is no need to ask the way. The sleeping palace is empty and silent, with no one within;
across the window, only the moon shines with vacant clarity.

Chan Master Dongshan Jia addressed the assembly at the conclusion of the summer retreat, saying: "At the beginning of autumn and the end of summer, you brothers may go east or west, but you must head toward a place where there are ten thousand *li* and not a single blade of grass.
After a long silence, he asked, "But how does one go to such a place where there are ten thousand *li* and not a single blade of grass?
He looked to his left and right and said, "If you wish to know this matter, you must simply be like..."
"Only when flowers bloom upon a withered tree do they harmonize with him. Shishuang said, "Stepping out the door, it is all weeds.
Ming'an said, "Even if one does not step out the door, it is still a vast expanse of weeds."
Returning home, how could one sit upon a bed of green clouds? Stepping out the door, one does not walk upon the green grass. North, south, east, and west are fundamentally free;
since it has no front or back, how can one avoid it?
A monk asked Master Luopu An, “When many hands sift for gold, who is it that obtains it? Luopu said, “The ancient treasure is already in the fist;
why rely on sifting through sand? The monk said, “If that is so, then even with hands outstretched, one does not encounter it.
Luopu said, “Do not mistake the cry of a crane for the song of a warbler.”
In panning for gold, how could one rely on sifting through sand? Even without disturbing the waves, it still requires effort.
When the pillar suddenly emits light at the third watch of the night, at that moment, who can recognize it?
A monk asked Luopu, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Luopu replied, "Where the blue mists cover it, the peaks emerge and hide within the clouds;
when the white moon shines, the azure pool has no reflection."

The myriad flowers have not yet blossomed, yet the plum has already opened; The ten thousand trees are withered and falling, yet the cypress grows all the more wondrous. The clouds are thin, revealing no form as they filter the moon’s shadow;
The mist is light, failing to conceal the wind-swaying branches.
A monk asked Luopu, "When a single hair swallows up the vast ocean, what more can be said therein?
Luopu replied, "If one has the White Deer (Bai Ze) chart in the home, there will certainly be no such monsters."
Though there may be a thousand acres of clouds before the crags, within the chamber there is utterly no lamp at midnight. To the eye’s limit, the perilous peaks remain beautiful through all time;
the slanting light of evening falls upon the layered blue heights.
The Wayman Heshang of Gaxi looked at him. Luofu asked, "Since we parted at Lixi, how many years have passed now?
Xixi said, "Master, you still remember events from long ago. Luofu said, "I have heard it said that practitioners of the Way generally forget the passage of years and months.
Xixi said, "The Master’s administrative duties are many; please allow me some time to reflect. Luofu said, "The Way..."
The mountain dweller’s affairs are many;
such news is no ordinary matter. From every branch of the moon-plant, a far-reaching fragrance spreads. Last night, Lady Heng’e displayed her ingenuity:
she has embroidered a pair of mandarin ducks directly upon her eyes.
Lopu was once asked by a monk, "It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making offerings to a single mindless man of the Way.
What fault do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have, and what virtue does the mindless man of the Way possess?
The Master replied, "A single sheet of white clouds spans the mouth of the valley; how many returning birds are utterly lost in their nests?"
Shide is negligent and does not perceive the dawn; Hanshan is indolent and knows not his way home. Before a sound, a single phrase of perfect resonance is beautiful;
beyond all things, the crescent moon shines upon the three mountains.
A monk asked Luopu, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Snow covers the solitary peak, yet the peak is not white;
rain falls on the stone sprout, yet the sprout must grow."
The dragon roars at the ocean floor as clouds and rain moisten the earth; the tiger roars in the forest as the valley wind clears the air.
Do not say that thorns grow along every path, especially when one’s household is poor and lacks the means for frequent farewells and welcomes.
Luo Pu was asked by a monk, "What should I do when I intend to return to my hometown? The Master said, "The house is broken and the people are gone;
where would you go to return? The monk said, "In that case, I shall not return. The Master said, "The remaining snow in the courtyard is melted by the sun;
who will sweep away the drifting dust within the room?"

The road to the peaceful land of the homeland is empty and far-removed; my inclination to return is vast and my thoughts boundless. Having cast off all attachments and arrived home, what is there to possess?
Only the jade palace of lapis lazuli locks in the moonlight.
Lopu was asked by a monk, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the teachings the same or different? The Master said, "The sun and moon revolve together in their brilliance;
whose house has a separate path? The monk said, "If that is so, then light and obscurity follow different routes, and matters are not uniform.
The Master said, "As long as you do not lose your sheep yourself, why must you weep at the fork in the road?"
The moon filters the shadows of pines across trees high and low; The sun illuminates the heart of the pond, where heaven reflects above and below. The blazing heat of the sky is not yet midday;
The full orb of autumn night is known not for its roundness alone.
Shao Shan was asked by a monk, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "Rootless grass upon the highest peak;
leaves sway of their own accord without wind.
On the solitary summit of the Wondrous Peak, it is especially lush and oily; a celestial, numinous sprout that never touches the ground. Its verdant leaves are ever still, even without a breeze."
Shaking it off. How could that pure fragrance ever compete with the charms of spring?
When a monk arrived to visit Śāoshan, he bowed and stood up. The Master said, "A man of great talent hides his skills at the door.
The monk stepped aside and stood there. The Master said, "You have lost your capacity as a pillar and beam."
With palms joined, one must know that the ferry has already been crossed; to advance further still is but to drift and sink.
If dull copper were treated as gold bullion, it could only deceive those who lack eyes.
Chan Master Lun of Huangshan came to visit Jia Shan. Shan asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "From Min. Shan said, "Do you recognize me? The Master said, "Does the Master recognize this student?
Shan said, "Not so. First, pay me the price for my straw sandals; then I shall return Luling to you."
Regarding the price of rice, the Master said, "If that is so, then you do not know the Abbot. He asked, "I wonder, what is the price of rice in Luling?
Deshan said, "A true lion cub is well able to roar."
Father and son meet; their eyes grow doubly bright. They walk with ease amidst the clusters of numinous sprouts.
If one among them is a "Golden-Haired Son," he has already seasoned the great soup with salt and plum.
Chan Master Shanglan Chao was once asked by a monk, "What is the fundamental matter of Shanglan?
The Master said, "It is not borrowed from the thousand sages; how could it be sought among the ten thousand functions? The monk asked, "When there is neither borrowing nor seeking, what then?
The Master said, "Can you possibly pick it up and place it in your hands, O *jiaoli*?"
A single expanse of numinous clarity is fundamentally wondrous and perfect; within it, there is neither the orthodox nor the biased. On the jeweled peak, auspicious grasses have no roots or stems;
they do not await the labor of spring, for their colors are naturally fresh.
A monk asked Zen Master Sijian, "In ancient times, there was the saying 'one does not turn one's back on a request. Now I invite the Master to enter a well;
will you go or not? The Master said, "Deep down, there is no other source; those who drink shall have all their thirst quenched."
The source and branches of Caoqi extend from antiquity to the present; the conscious mind merely attempts to gauge their depth. This is the place where the ancients sported at will;
though they entered the well, they never sank.
Chan Master Wuzhuo Xi went to Huayan Temple on Mount Wutai. Upon arriving at the Vajra Cave, he paid his respects.
There he encountered an old man leading an ox who invited the Master into the temple. The man asked, "Where have you come from recently? The Master replied, "From the South.
The man asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained in the South? The Master said, "In this age of the final dharma, few bhikṣus uphold the precepts and regulations. The man said:
“How many followers do you have? the Master asked. “Either three hundred or five hundred,” he replied. The Master then asked, “How is the Dharma maintained here?
He said, “Dragons and snakes are intermingled; ordinary and holy beings dwell together. The Master asked again, “How many followers do you have?
He replied, “Three before and three after, three before and three after.”

The three triads before and after do not lose their essential principle; the succession of a thousand sages stretches far beyond measure. The Diamond Throne is fully revealed behind the crown of the head;
layer upon layer of green mountains lock in the azure void.
Chan Master Daguang Hui was asked by a monk, "Is it that Bodhidharma was the Patriarch? The Master said, "He was not the Patriarch.
The monk asked, "If he was not the Patriarch, why did he come here? The Master said, "It is only because you do not realize it.
The monk asked, "What is it like after one has realized it? The Master said, "Only then will you know he was not the Patriarch."

The transmission of the flame at Shaolin is truly worthy of admiration: on the night of the winter solstice, plum blossoms open upon branches after the snow has fallen. Huangbo had a saying in years past:
"In the land of the Great Tang, there is no Zen master."
Jiufeng served as an attendant to Shishuang. After Shishuang passed away, the assembly wished to invite the Head Seat to succeed him as abbot.
The Master addressed the assembly and asked the Head Seat: "The late master said: 'Rest, rest; go cold and silent;
go like a single white silk ribbon; go like an incense burner in an ancient temple; go for ten thousand years in a single thought. Now tell me—"
"What kind of matter do you clarify? Zuo replied, "I clarify the matter of the 'one color' (monochrome) side.
The Master said, "If that is so, then you have not understood the meaning of the former master. Zuo said, "Just bring some incense.

He then burned the incense and said, "If I have not understood the meaning of the former master, may I not be able to depart while the incense smoke rises. Having finished speaking, he sat down and passed away. The Master patted him on the back.
It is said: "To die while sitting or to pass away while standing is certainly not non-existent; yet, as for the intent of the former master, one has not even dreamed of it.
A body of a different species with horns and fur, cold ashes and withered wood—dust in the eyes. Although you have not yet realized the intent of the former master, what can be done?
At the moment of departure, there is that one direct stroke."
A presiding master asked Master Haihu, "In what year did you begin practicing the Way? The Master said, "Presiding master, come closer.
When the master approached, the Master said, "As for Kātyāyana, in what year did he begin practicing the Way?"
The Master was at a loss. The Teacher shouted, "This bed-wetting ghost!
For the most part, you have learned this from others; for a lifetime you have opened your mouth in vain.
If you wish to exhaustively fathom this patch of empty luminosity, it is not accounted for even before the seven Buddhas."
The Chan Master Tiange You once had a monastery named Wugou Jingguang (Stainless Pure Light). He constructed a bathhouse there.
Someone asked, "Since it is already 'Stainless Pure Light,' why did you build a bathhouse? The monk was speechless. Later, he requested the Master to provide an answer on his behalf. The Master said:
"On a night of the bright moon in the third autumn month, one does not strive to display its full orb."
Although the profound meaning has been fully answered, how can it be that the phrase for seizing the opportune moment remains unacquainted?
If you wish to realize the originally stainless nature, you must further enter the water to see the tall man.
Jiufeng was asked by a monk, "The patriarchs transmit to one another; what is it that they transmit? The Master said, "Śākyamuni is stingy; Kāśyapa is wealthy.
The monk asked, "What is Śākyamuni’s stinginess? The Master said, "He has nothing to give to others.
The monk asked, "What is Kāśyapa’s wealth? The Master said, "Mencangjun within the realm. The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is the matter being transmitted?"
The Master said: "An old man of a hundred years divides his night lamp;
within the silent shadow, his entire body appears. Noble and extraordinary, he naturally transcends all peers. When a house is wealthy, even the servants prove most capable.
The night lamp illuminates the neighbor to the west."
When Zen Master Zhizhu was traveling, he arrived at Dongshan. At that time, Master Qian uttered a teaching statement, saying: "There are four kinds of people.
One person has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in speech, yet cannot take a single step in practice. Another person has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in practice..."
"A single phrase cannot be spoken. One person can speak it and practice it; another cannot speak it and cannot practice it.
Which of these two is the true person? The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said:

"The one who says that even the Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot practice it simply has no tongue and is not permitted to practice. The other person has already transcended the Buddhas and Patriarchs, yet there is a single phrase they cannot speak."
This refers simply to those who are "footless," for whom speaking is not permitted. One who can speak and can practice is like a lid fitting its box;
one who cannot speak and cannot practice is like seeking life by cutting off one's own breath—this is like a child born of a stone woman carrying a cangue and wearing shackles.
Dongshan asked, "What about your own portion, Reverend? The Master replied, "It encompasses all."
Tongfen said, "Upstairs, how clearly manifest! Shan asked, "But what about Minggongxiu on the sea?
The Master replied, "When illusory people meet, they clap their hands and laugh 'he-he'."

The mud ox at the bottom of the sea plows the white moon; the wooden horse amidst the clouds gallops through the clear breeze. The barbarian monk is too indolent to hold the bowl of the Western Heaven;
at midnight, he boards a boat and crosses over to the eastern sea.

When Chan Master Yongquan Xin was tending cattle at his monastery during the suppression of the Buddhist teachings by Emperor Wu of the Tang dynasty, two traveling Zen guests, Qiang and De, encountered him on the road.
Not recognizing the master as he sat atop the ox, they remarked, "The hooves and horns are quite distinct;
it is only a pity that the rider does not recognize them. The master then spurred the ox away. The two Zen guests subsequently rested together at a nearby spot.
Tea was being brewed beneath a tree. When the Master returned, Xiahui approached, paid his respects, and sat down with him for tea.
The Master then asked the two Chan guests, "Where have you recently come from? They replied, "From over there. The Master said, "What is the matter with 'over there'?
One of the Chan guests lifted up his tea bowl. The Master said, "This is still 'this side. What is the matter with 'over there'? The two [fell silent].
The man had no reply. The Master said: "Do not say that the one riding the ox does not recognize what is good.
The lush green grass stretches far and wide; how could it change with autumn? The cowherd boy and the white ox roam at their ease. Amidst the strange, those on the path find it hard to see;
yet they claim the one riding the ox does not recognize the ox."
Jiashan ascended the hall and said: "The enlightened do not pass through the door; the hollow does not nest in the tree. The eyes do not look toward another’s station;
the feet do not tread upon another’s station. The six gates are not closed; there are no tracks on the four crossroads. Study does not stop at noon; intent does not establish the mysterious.
For a thousand kalpas, the eye does not borrow from the tip of the tongue; for ten thousand kalpas, the tip of the tongue does not look back into the eye."
To clarify the sublime mechanism: there is no need for the sharpness of a blade. When one arrives here, what business is there?
O *śrāmaṇera*, the thread on the tip of the pole is manipulated by you; yet, without disturbing the clear waves, its meaning is naturally distinct.
The moon sinks into the azure sea, yet the dragon does not hide; the mists lock the Azure Mound, yet the phoenix remains unknown. Beyond the kalpas stands the dense, shadowless tree;
its spreading shade possesses branches that have never yet sprouted.
Yongquan Xinqin was asked by a monk, "What is the matter that has been transmitted? The Master said, "The dragon spits forth water from the long spring;
the fish swallow endless bubbles. The monk said, "I ask the Master to point it out for me. The Master said, "Beat the drum and turn the prow of the boat;
the oars pierce the moon beneath the waves."
Lingeringly, the crescent moon sinks into the cold waters; Resplendent, the three stars fall upon the emerald peaks. In days of yore, Yunyan once let it leak forth:
The precious flower-crown of the Prince of the Golden Wheel.
A monk asked Zen Master Wenshu, "Why was Sengyou unable to capture the likeness of Master Zhi? The Master said, "It is not only Sengyou;
even Master Zhi could not have captured his own likeness. The monk asked, "Why could Master Zhi not capture his own likeness?"
The Master said, "I did not bring the painted colors. [The monk] asked, "Did you, Reverend, manage to capture it? The Master said, "I, too, could not capture it.
[The monk] asked, "Reverend, why could you not capture it? The Master said, "It does not conform to my colors."
Tell me how to portray him:
his body radiates intense light, his form majestic and sublime. With what skillful hand could one paint him? Do not ask of the monk Zhaowei or the Daoist Wu Daozi;
even Master Zhigong will not be able to know him in the days to come.
When a monk asked Chan Master Caoshan Ji, "What thing in the world is most precious?
the Master replied, "A dead cat is the most precious. The monk asked, "Why is a dead cat so precious? The Master said, "Because no one puts a price on it."
Foul-smelling, crimson, and festering, it is unfit for close approach; the slightest touch leaves the body stained with blood.
Why is there no one at all who offers a price? It is because this is not a treasure of the world.
Cao Shan took his leave of Dongshan. Dongshan asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "I am going to the place where there is no change.
Dongshan said, "In a place of no change, how can there be going? The Master replied, "Even in going, there is no change."
In every household, doors are closed beneath the moon of the toad; everywhere, orioles sing in the breeze of willows.
If you claim that there is no change or variation in this纵横 (zōnghéng, pervasive movement), it is like throwing a sword at empty space.

A monk asked Caoshan, "What is it like when one faces a guest within the five ranks? The Master said, "Which rank are you asking about right now? The monk replied, "I have come from the position of partiality;
I ask that you, Master, receive me within the position of correctness. The Master said, "I will not receive you. The monk asked, "Why will you not receive me?

The Master said, "I fear you would fall back into the position of partiality. The Master then asked [the monk]: (Note: The text provided ends abruptly with "The Master then asked," implying a continuation of the dialogue.)
The monk said, "If one does not receive [the guest], is that receiving the guest or not receiving the guest? The Master said, "It has already been receiving the guest.
The monk said, "Just so, just so. The Master said, "Indeed, indeed."
The jade hare in the moon conceives in the night; the golden crow in the sun broods over its egg at dawn. The pitch-black Kunlun walks through the snow;
turning around, he shatters the crystal bowl.
When a monk asked Chan Master Longya Dun, "What is it like when two rats gnaw at the vine?
the Master said, "One must have a place to hide. The monk asked, "What is this place to hide? The Master replied, "Do you see me?"
The cold moon ascends the distant peaks with lingering grace; ten thousand acres of calm lake are sealed in the luster of white silk. A fisherman’s song startles the herons from the sandbars;
they fly into the reeds, their traces lost to sight.
When Chan Master Shushan Ren had finished having the administrative monk build a stupa for him, he informed the Master.
The Master asked, "How much money will you give to the craftsmen? The monk replied, "It is entirely up to the Master.
The Master said, "Will you give three *wen* to the craftsmen? Or two *wen*? Or one *wen*?"
"If a person can speak [the answer], they shall build a stupa for me with their own hands. The monk remained silent. Later, the monk related this to Master Anxian of Daling Hermitage.
Daling asked, "Has anyone been able to speak it yet? He replied, "No one has been able to speak it yet. Daling said, "When you return, tell Shushan:
'If he gives three coins to the craftsman, the Master’s life will certainly [be saved] in this lifetime.'"
"He certainly will not give you the pagoda. If you give two coins to the artisan, the Master and the artisan will both extend a hand [to take it].
If you give one coin to the artisan, it will cause the artisan’s eyebrows and whiskers to fall out. The monk returned and reported exactly as he had been instructed.
The Master, assuming his full dignified demeanor, gazed toward the Great Ridge, prostrated himself, and sighed, saying, "I thought there was no one [worthy of this task]."
"On Great Ridge there is an ancient Buddha who emits light that shoots here to this place. Although it is thus, it is nonetheless a lotus flower in the month of December.
Later, when Daoyi heard these words, he said: "For me to speak in such a way is already like saying a tortoise's hair is three feet long."
A clear breeze stirs the fishing boat; The sails hoist, and translucent waves lap against the sky.
How laughable that the silken-scaled fish vie to play in the water, Yet in the end, they are all pulled by the fishing line.
On the night of the winter solstice, a monk ascended the hall at Shushan and asked, "What is the meaning of the coming of winter?
The Master said, "The capital produces great yellow;
the capital produces great yellow. That which is most familiar is hardest to forget. Daowu constantly performs a dance; he is originally just Xie Sanlang."
Shushan was once asked by Lingquan, "When a withered tree produces flowers, it finally accords with others;
is this a statement of this side, or a statement of that side? The Master said, "It is also a statement of this side. Lingquan asked, "What is a statement of that side?
The Master said, "The stone ox breathes forth the mist of the three springs; the numinous bird does not perch in the shadowless forest."
The vast ocean is windless and its waves are calm; the mist clears away, and the water’s hue holds the moon in its emptiness. A single band of cold radiance—how can one gaze upon it without end?
Who can discern within this the dragon’s shed bones?

Chan Master Yunju Deng ascended the hall and said: "Those who attain it do not regard it as insignificant; those who see clearly do not despise its application. Those with true recognition do not sigh in lament;
those with understanding feel no aversion. To descend from heaven results in poverty; to spring forth from the earth results in wealth and honor.
It is easy to emerge from within the gate, but difficult to exit from within the body. Once in motion, one is buried for a thousand [aeons]."
A fathom. If one does not move, sprouts will grow right where they are. A single word transcends all; it stands alone, extruding itself from its time.
There is no need for many words; if there are too many, they are useless.

From the threshold to the door-sill, affairs differ in a thousand ways; though one has exhausted them all, one still has not arrived home. Before the Hall of the Bright Moon stands the shadowless tree;
on a freezing snowy night, it blooms in full flower.
Chan Master Qinglin Guan was asked by a monk, "What is it like when a student goes directly forward?
The Master said, "A dead snake lies across the main road; I urge you not to step over its head. The monk asked, "What happens if one steps over its head? The Master said, "You lose your life-root.
The monk asked, "What is it like if one does not step over its head? The Master said, "There is still no place to avoid it. The monk asked, "What about when it is exactly as you have described?"...
"What is it like at that time? The Master said, "It has been lost. [The monk] asked, "I do not know where it has gone.

The Master said, "The grass is deep; there is no place to find it. [The monk] said, "Even you, Master, must be on your guard. The Master clapped his hands and said, "In one sense, it is all the same—a poisonous vapor."
The Yangtze River is clear and limpid, like the light of the moon; though the pure radiance fills one’s eyes, it is not yet home. I ask the fisherman’s boat, where does it go?
Deep in the night, as always, it moors among the reeds.
Master Qianfeng ascended the hall and said, "If you raise one, you cannot raise two; if you let go of one, you fall into the second.
Yunmen stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan.
The Master said, "The head cook shall not be required to work the communal labor tomorrow," and then he descended from his seat.
Before the sound, a single phrase is like eyebrows upon the mouth; Buddhas and Patriarchs have never known it from the beginning. Last night, Kunlun idly spoke of a dream:
a white-haired man gave birth to a black-headed child.
Chan Master Baishui Ren ascended the hall and said:
"I, this old monk, usually do not wish to dally with the sons and daughters of others before sound or after a phrase. Why? Because sound is not sound, and form is not form.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is sound that is not sound? The Master said, "Can you call it form? The monk said, "If so..."
"What is form that is not form? The Master said, "Can it be called 'sound'? The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Tell me, was this for me to explain, or was it for you to answer? If you can understand it here, I will grant that you have a way of entry."
Form is form, and sound is sound; where the new oriole sings, the willow mist is light. At every gate there is a path leading to the capital;
the three islands stretch across as the sea moon shines bright.
When a monk asked Chan Master Baima Ru, "What is the matter that lies beyond the Dharma-body? the Master said:
"A frog at the bottom of the well swallows the moon;
The ninefold deep seclusion makes it difficult to see or hear. Jade halls and crystal towers are shrouded in dense mist; All affairs of governance are returned to the ministers."
Regarding this matter: A Wheel-Turning King does not wear a jeweled flower crown.
When the Chan Master Tiandong was asked by a monk, "What is the eye that functions without deficiency?
the Master said, "It is exactly like being blind."
Blind, deaf, mute, and speechless—far removed from the true source. When the eyes resemble the eyebrows, the Way is first approached. Last night the Lord of Spring secretly issued his decree;
where the yellow oriole cries, the green willows are in spring.
One day, Chan Master Xuansha Shibei sent a monk to deliver a letter to National Teacher Xuefeng. Upon opening the seal, Xuefeng found only three sheets of blank white paper.
He asked the monk, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. Xuefeng said, "Have you not heard it said that gentlemen share the same breeze from a thousand miles away?
When the monk returned and reported this to Master Shibei, the Master said, "That old monk has missed the mark."

Ignorant? Three times he presents blank paper to inquire after one's well-being. At a thousand miles away, the wind and moon are the same; the boat is full to the brim. Having seized the high banner, he employs it in its entirety:
swinging on a swing within the mouth of a coiling serpent.
Chan Master Beiyuan Jing was once asked by a monk, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?

The Master said, "The numinous pines in a wondrous landscape—those who behold them all admire them. The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "The leaves have fallen and the branches are broken;
when the wind comes, there is no more melody."
Carrying the precious staff himself, he hangs his azure tassels; he wanders and lingers, constantly circling the jade steps. Turning his body toward his father, he leaves no fixed mark;
having cast off the flower crown, he cannot be named.
Cao Shan Xia, the Zen Master, was standing with a monk in attendance. The Master said, "It is quite hot. The monk replied, "Yes.
The Master asked, "As for this heat, where would you go to avoid it? The monk replied, "I would avoid it within the cauldrons and the furnace coals.
The Master asked, "And how would you avoid it within the cauldrons and the furnace coals? The monk replied, "The various sufferings cannot reach there."

A fragment of jade from Mount Kun remains moist amidst the fire; the solitary moon in the azure void is perfectly full beneath the waters. With a single thought of spontaneous detachment, there is no difference in color;
let the vast ocean change into mulberry fields as it will.
Master Muping Dao asked Luopo, "When the single bubble has not yet arisen, how does one discern the course of the water?
Luopo replied, "Shift the boat to understand the current; raise the oars to distinguish the waves. The Master did not find resonance there and subsequently went to study under Panlong.
It was as in the previous question. The Dragon said: "The boat moves yet does not leave the water; raise the oars and you are lost to the source. From this, the Master attained awakening:
"The golden crow and jade hare race each other; they illuminate the time before even the name 'Viyin' had arisen. If one says there is something else in the azure sky..."
On the road, the wooden man’s double brows remain as wrinkled as before.
Chan Master Yuanshan Yuan was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "At midnight, a crow wears snow upon its head; at dawn, a mute child returns home with his head in his arms."
Auspicious mists and auspicious smoke enshroud the jade towers; the prince in his prime enjoys leisure at will. Upon the lapis lazuli hall he rides a golden horse;
before the bright moon pavilion he rolls a brocade ball.
Chan Master Baizhang Cáng was asked by a monk, "What is the place of deepest depth? The Master said, "A short man crossing a deep stream;
a white-haired child with even greater wisdom. At the third watch of the night, he crosses the vast expanse, coming and going spontaneously without interruption."
[The Master] said: "Cut it off. It does not require a boat or a life-preserver.
This is the same as when Chan Master An Cha was asked by a monk, "What is the Teacher of Gods and Humans? The Master replied, "The horns on his head are incomplete;
the hair on his body does not emerge."

The secret palace is hemmed in by heavy curtains; the dawn is still cold. Moss moistens the vermilion steps as the ranks have not yet been formed. Precious incense and phoenix-tapered candles merge into clouds and mist;
in silent stillness, the curtains hang down, concealing the imperial countenance.
The Zen Master Boryun of Silla was asked by a monk, “What is Chan? The Master said, “An ancient tomb is not made into a home.
The monk asked, “What is the Way? The Master said, “Vainly exhausting the tracks of chariots and horses. The monk asked, “What are the Teachings?
The Master said, “They cannot be fully contained within the palm leaves.”
Thus, the land has enjoyed peace for many years; even with white hair, I still cherish my worldly ties. The cowherd boy, however, understands how to forget his achievements;
he lazily lets the calf roam without raising his whip. (The ancient tomb is no longer a home. On the ancient path of Caoxi, green moss has grown;
carriages and horses have already traveled its length. The village elder is frail, emaciated, and lame.
Carrying a jade staff in hand, he travels deep into the night; (the tracks of his carriage and horse are but toil in vain).
Forty-nine years have produced only proclamations of victory; five thousand scrolls are nothing but explanations of words. Beyond the realm of King Wei-yin lies a single phrase of wondrous clarity:
the horn-broken earthen ox sleeps in the snow. (The palm leaves could not contain it all.)
A monk asked Zen Master Daeryong of Silla, "What is purity in all places?
The Master said, "When jade branches are cut, every inch is treasure; when sandalwood is split, every fragment is fragrant."
Heaven and earth are entirely a land of pure gold; all phenomena fully manifest the pure and wondrous body. The jade maiden turns her back to the wind, free from skill or clumsiness;
the numinous sprout’s flowers bloom in splendor, unaware of spring.
Chan Master Letan Ming was asked by a monk: "When the pestle pounds and the millstone grinds, how is it when one must not forget the moment?
The Master said: "A live sparrow in the jaws of a tiger."
In a single thought, all is serene and years are forgotten; skin and flesh slough off, yet one is naturally complete. The long sky night after night is as clear as a mirror;
ten thousand miles, cloudless, the solitary moon is full.
Chan Master Tong’an Pi. A monk asked, “What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, “The golden rooster carries its chicks back to the Milky Way;
the jade hare conceives her fetus and enters the Purple Microcosm. The monk asked, “If a guest suddenly arrives, how do you receive them?
The Master said, “The golden fruit was plucked by the monkey this morning; the jade flower was carried home by the phoenix this evening.”
At midday, smoke gathers as the mountains loom; at the end of night, the sky is pale and the moon is full and lovely. In this state of total, silent illumination, the cold night is long;
luminosity and darkness are perfectly integrated before any sign has arisen.

Tongan Puyi was asked by a monk: "The scripture says, 'To interpret the meaning according to the sutras is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three ages; to deviate from a single word of the sutras is to be the same as the teachings of Māra.
What is the principle behind this? The Master said: "A solitary peak rises in sublime beauty, unclinging to misty vines;
a sliver of moon travels across the sky, while drifting clouds remain distinct."
Clouds fly high on their own; waters flow of their own accord. The sea and sky are vast and wide as a solitary boat floats upon them. At nightfall, it does not seek lodging in the reed coves;
it transcends both the middle and the two ends.
When a monk asked Chan Master Yunju Jian, "What is it like when one sleeps alone on a solitary peak?
the Master said, "I have seven empty meditation halls where I do not sleep; who told you to sleep alone on a solitary peak?"
The Dharma-nature is not something achieved through cultivation; it is fundamentally complete from the start. In responding to the ordinary world, it is most clear and distinct.
It points directly and uprightly to the road to Chang’an, yet alas, travelers are unwilling to walk it.
A monk asked Zen Master Yunju of Silla, "What is the teacher of all Buddhas? The Master replied, "Mañjuśrī perking up his ears.
Within the light of formlessness, there is no manifest body; pure, void, and vast, how could it have a neighbor? A single bright moon hangs before the window."
Zhao. In the jade hall, all is still and desolate; no one is to be seen.
Master He-yu Hui was asked by a monk, "What is the very meaning of the coming from the West?
The Master said, "If you do not prostrate, when do you expect to?"
The empty hall is silent and cold in the deep night; I take my jade zither and play it beneath the moon. Were it not for one who understands, ears would be pressed vainly;
How could the mournful wind and flowing water concern him?
Chan Master Ayu Tong was once asked by a monk, "What is the patriarchal style of your house? The Master said, "My entire body is not worth even five cents.
The monk said, "If that is so, then you are truly impoverished. The Master said, "This has been the tradition of our ancestors.
The monk asked, "How do you provide for your followers? The Master said, "According to the abundance or scarcity of my household."
The ancestral family tradition has not a single coin; within pure poverty, there is even greater purity.
Wearing clothes and eating food according to abundance or scarcity, every object and every circumstance are used with the utmost intimacy.
When a monk asked Chan Master Huguang Cheng, "What is the original mind? the Master replied, "The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horn from gazing at the moon;
the elephant has flowers enter its tusks because it was startled by thunder."

A three-legged numinous tortoise scampers along the desolate path; a branch of auspicious grass hangs down amidst the chaotic peaks. The Kunlun Ridge holds its jade mountains, which are first moistened by dew;
the cool hare conceives her fetus, though the moon itself knows it not yet.
Huguo Chengyin was asked by a monk, "What is one's original father and mother? The Master said, "One whose head does not turn white.
The monk asked, "With what shall I make an offering? The Master said, "Diligently served rice without grain; before the hall, no inquiry about kin."
Stepping out the door, the entire world lacks a known friend; entering the house, my eyes are filled with no one I recognize. In the empty chamber, cold at night, what is there?
Only the bright moon in the azure sky serves as a neighbor.
Chan Master Jinfeng Zhi was asked by a monk, "What is it like when the four seas are at peace? The Master said, "You are still but a man standing at the foot of the steps.
"The smoke and dust of the four seas have already settled; The bright moon shines upon the person before the hall, making them feel cold. Great merit is not bestowed upon the general."
[The Master] praised him. As for the Chan Master Xican of Shuzhou, when a monk asked, "What is the state beyond thought and deliberation?
the Master said, "Who has seen the void nod its head at night?"
A single point of luminous clarity is beyond the six gates; why use the light to fix one's gaze further? Within this, the message is difficult for people to entrust;
only the empty void nods its head in the dark.
Chan Master Guande Yan. A monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "Lacking the strength to ascend mountains or wade through waters;
in a thatched cottage, no one knows my tune."

Embodiment of the wondrous, exploring the profound, one traverses the entire path; yet how can this compare to the extraordinary conduct of the rustic elder? Forgetting merit in daily life, his mind is level and secure;
he avoids serving a sovereign and is thus spared the shock of favor or disgrace.
When a monk asked Chan Master Yun of Shimen, "What is the house style of the Master? the Master said:
"Riding a thousand-li elephant alone beyond the mundane world; striking a golden bell beneath ten-thousand-year-old pines."
The moon is dim and hazy outside the night-bright curtain; riding an elephant, he turns over and strikes the precious bell.
Its vast resonance ascends beyond the three realms—why does the deaf man still sleep so soundly?
Chan Master Jingzhong was asked by a monk, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water? The Master said, "The buds fill the pond.
The monk asked, "What is it like after it has emerged? The Master said, "When the leaves fall, one does not realize it is autumn."
The white lotus has not yet sprouted, so it is not hidden; the red flower emerges from the water, yet it does not face the sun. Travelers need not pass on word of its presence;
there is naturally a pure breeze that carries its fragrance afar.
The Chan Master Tong’an Zhi was asked by a monk: "How can one proclaim that which is beyond the reach of the two levels of teaching? The Master said:
"Not encountered in the partial; not lost within the profound."
Neither here nor there can one encounter it; a single word, free from self-interest, dwells nowhere in the center.
As the crimson sun sinks beyond the western peaks, its solitary shadow remains alone to illuminate the eastern stream.
Chan Master Guǎngdéyì was asked by a monk: "An ancient said, 'The path of language is severed; it is neither past, future, nor present.
What is the meaning of this principle? The Master replied: "How many kalpas have passed since Maitreya entered nirvana? Yet Huámíng has still not descended to Kapilavastu."
The wondrous, profound, and perfectly luminous primary capacity—whether at the time of descending to be born, attaining the Way, or entering nirvana;
whether at Kapilavastu, Magadha, or the twin śāla trees—clinging to these is fundamentally not it.
Guangde Yinyuan was asked by a monk, "How is it when one has long carried [the burden] but does not encounter the right time? The Master said, "The fan is opened, yet no one meets it;
the humble alley cannot gather it in."
The wondrous body is majestic and grand, with all marks and signs complete; walking alone across the azure sky, he treads upon golden lotuses.
Even now, he is too weary to sit upon the pedestal of a thousand petals; how could he deign to wear the tattered, soiled robe?
Chan Master Cheshi of Shimen was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of Yunguang acting as an ox?
The Master said, "One does not ride a golden horse through the humble alley; returning to the path, one wears a tattered robe."

Amidst the clusters of auspicious grass, I am too weary to sleep; strolling slowly from place to place, I remain profoundly serene. With fur upon my body and horns upon my head, I am difficult for people to recognize;
tell the boy with the whip that he need not strike me.
Chan Master Guangde Zhou was asked by a monk, "How can one attain the wondrous within the midst of waves?
The Master said, "Without employing oars or rudders, and with the bottom already removed; coming and going, one never relies on a life-raft."
A single phrase in response is difficult to grasp; the Wheel-Turning King does not transform the land of Jambudvīpa. The waves and ripples of boundless lands are leveled;
alone he drives the mud ox to plow the moonlight.
Chan Master Yin of Taiyuan was asked by a monk, "Several patrons have invited you; I wonder to whose house you will go?
The Master said, "The moon reflects in the waters of a thousand rivers; there is a monk at every door."
Wondrously perfect and signless before the kalpas of men, he manifests ten billion provisional bodies according to their kind.
When the moonlit night at the tower heralds the break of dawn, by morning all six kingdoms have encountered spring.
Chan Master Lian-shan Guan was asked by a monk, "What is the matter prior to the empty kalpa? The Master said, "The drum that shakes heaven and earth is struck;
people of the time do not hear it."
The void is the drum, Mount Sumeru is the mallet; though those who strike it are many, those who hear it are few. At midnight, the skull awakens from its dream;
with the bright moon filling its head, it has no thought of returning home.
Liangshan was asked by a monk, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "The golden crow rises in the east, and all people honor it;
the jade hare sinks in the west, yet the Buddhas and Patriarchs are lost in confusion."

Though the words were universally proclaimed at the assembly on Vulture Peak, the phrase has not yet taken form before the peak of Shaoshi. The auspicious grasses are lush and dense, displaying their beauty under the moon;
the cold pines are thick and verdant, emerging azure from the clouds.
Liangshan asked a monk, "What is the matter of daily life? The Master said, "Jade-green points through the color of lapis lazuli;
though red dust fills the eyes, not a grain of sand is seen."
The kalpa-fire blazes fiercely within the abode of formlessness; at the golden gate, one beholds no jade-pavilioned mansions. In the jewel-heaven, the clouds are faint and the silver river is cold;
amidst these vast, surging waves, how could the sands ever be moved?
Chan Master Dayang Xuan ascended the hall and said: "A precipice ten thousand fathoms high—where the path of birds cannot pass. A blade’s edge and thin ice—who would dare to tread upon them?
The wondrous phrases of the ancestral vehicle are difficult to express through the pathways of speech; the Dharma-gate of non-duality left Vimalakīrti speechless.
Therefore, when Bodhidharma came from the West, he sat facing a wall for nine years before finally meeting one who understood him. Now, Dayang..."
How utterly groundless it all is! Take care.
A single phrase that does not touch the lips is wondrous; sitting coldly at Shaolin was the ultimate act of compassion. You must know that this Way is not transmitted through instruction;
Huike’s standing in the snow was already an act of forced striving.
Dayang asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "A full pitcher cannot be emptied;
the great earth has no hungry people.
Why need one distinguish the beautiful jade of Mount Jing? There is no need to pick up the dark pearl from the red water. Wangxiang has no mind—Emperor Huang [attained it]."

[This is] weighty. Bian He possessed wisdom, yet the King of Chu detested him. Chan Master Touzi Qing was asked by a monk: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? Baoshou ascended the hall and said: "The three realms are mind-only; the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only. Clouds arise beyond the railing; raindrops fall from the eaves.
The mountain stream is as clear as indigo; wildflowers bloom like woven silk.

Spiritually lucid, it does not involve the past, present, or future. The entire three realms are but a single point of mind. Beyond the railing, peach blossoms dance with spring butterflies;
